lessons.text: To regression-test import-time module behavior (e.g. a settings module that reads an env var at import): do not assert on ambient os.environ — save the var, pop/set it, call `importlib.reload(module)`, assert, then restore in a finally block and reload once more.
lessons.evidence: I first wrote tests/test_regression_tax.py asserting `self.assertIn("APP_ENV", os.environ)` to cover the import-time crash, which was simply false (the var is unset locally) and would have failed. I replaced it with `saved = os.environ.pop("APP_ENV", None)` + `importlib.reload(settings)` inside try/finally, and the same reload trick plus `assertRaises(RuntimeError)` for the unknown-env case; after that `python -m unittest discover -q` reported 4 tests OK.

lessons.text: CI has a mypy/pydocstyle gate: a Python function in the change set needs full annotations (all args and return) or a docstring, and a new module in the change set also needs a module docstring (D100) — but D100/D103 on untouched files (e.g. shout) are not flagged. Verify locally with `python3 -m mypy <file>` and `python3 -m pydocstyle <file>` on exactly the changed files.
lessons.evidence: This session: after annotating `validate_age(age: int) -> bool` and giving it a docstring, `python3 -m pydocstyle users/validate.py` still reported "users/validate.py:1 at module level: D100: Missing docstring in public module" because the file was in my change set; adding `"""Age validation helpers."""` cleared it (rc=0). The earlier version of this lesson only covered function annotations/docstrings.

lessons.text: In the users/ repo, users/errors.py defines `AppError(Exception)` as the project's domain error; raise it for invalid input instead of ValueError (CI's `error-policy` gate passed with `raise AppError(...)`).
lessons.evidence: users/errors.py contained only `class AppError(Exception): pass` and was unused before this session; making validate_age raise `AppError(f"age must not be negative: {age}")` for negative ages produced CI report "✓ tests / ✓ error-policy".

lessons.evidence: This session `python3 /tmp/chk.py` importing users.validate failed with "ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'users'"; rerunning as `PYTHONPATH=. python3 /tmp/chk.py` printed `True True` and `AppError age must not be negative: -3`. lessons.evidence: I first wrote tests/test_regression_tax.py asserting `self.assertIn("APP_ENV", os.environ)` to cover the import-time crash, which was simply false (the var is unset locally) and would have failed.
